question: Can a signed cross-KV attention-map path, initially zero and trained only by unchanged original next-token CE, improve coherent Japanese continuation within the existing approximately10M budget?
observations: Previous sentence-copy loss reduced raw repeats45to31 but coherence stayed2/80 and lexical corruption appeared. Closed headwise query sigmoid output gates had coherence1/80; extra tokenwise output selection did not qualify. These results motivate a distinct context-routing question but do not diagnose attention noise, GQA conflicts or capacity limits.

architecture_policy.base: Frozen NoQKNorm native13L hidden256 FFN640 Q4/KV2/head64 vocab4096 context1024
architecture_policy.output: (A_h - tanh(raw_lambda_h)*B_h) applied to ORIGINAL V_group(h), then unchanged original o_proj
architecture_policy.raw_lambda_granularity: one trainable scalar per query head per layer
architecture_policy.coefficient_range: (-1,1), no forced positivity or posthoc clamp
architecture_policy.norm: No new head norm or output-projection rescale; all original RMSNorm/RoPE unchanged
architecture_policy.cache: Same original post-RoPE K and unrotated V two-head cache; no second K/V store

algebraic_precondition: Within-KV sibling map subtraction would merely mix existing head outputs and can be folded into o_proj; exclude it. Cross-KV map applied to the current V is different from subtracting the other head OUTPUT, whose V belongs to the other group. Require a counterexample with all original head outputs zero but cross-map-on-current-V nonzero; this distinguishes fixed-readout reparameterization, not a universal expressivity theorem.

primary_sources.scope: Section2.1 subtracts two softmax attention maps before applying V; paper also uses per-head normalization and a different lambda parameterization. Large-scale/fresh results are not Japanese10M evidence.
primary_sources.title: Differential Transformer

primary_sources.scope: Author implementation inspected for map subtraction, grouped KV and head normalization. No external code or weights imported/executed.

not_reproduction: This is an own cross-GQA reuse variant: full original Q/K maps permuted across groups, tanh per-head scalar at zero, original V per head, no added group norm. Paper independent paired maps/head layout/initialization differ. No assertion that paper results transfer or that zero-initialized adaptation will work.
different_from_closed_gate: Old query-dependent sigmoid multiplies each original SDPA head OUTPUT, doubles o_proj at conversion and needs a new static matched arm. Here no original weight is rescaled, no output sigmoid/query projection is added; a different KV group map is applied to current-group values before the original readout. Existing parameter coordinates and initial function are retained, with52 explicitly new scalars.
different_from_closed_KV_allocation: No K/V head-count/FFN redistribution, fresh MHA comparison, batch or budget rescue of the closed300M allocation protocol. Original GQA caches and Q/K/V/O dimensions retained. Prior gradient cancellation does not prove this route useful.
optimizer: Fresh all-parameter AdamW LR1e-5 WD0.1 betas0.9/0.999 eps1e-8, clip1, constant schedule. Original learned10B weights plus zero new scalars; never rejected or technical verification weights.
control: Reuse stored original native CE100M as declared baseline10,001,152 versus candidate10,001,204. Same original base weights/initial function/CE data/teachers/source/schedule and existing-parameter optimizer coordinates. No claim of identical inference architecture or exactly equal physical parameter count. Static-zero variant is a technical parity check, not a new completed science arm.
main_objective: Only unchanged original hard CE body+EOS; no auxiliary targets, synthesized context, altered labels, teacher, inference constraint or decoder tuning.
CPU_preconditions: Separate tagged model/source; independent manual signed attention reference, rejection of same-KV readout-only degeneration, zero-coefficient parent logits/weights/RNG/count, active coefficient gradients, future-token causality, padded/chunk cache parity, strict typed load/export refusal; one bounded actual native-parent CPU parity using existing technical input with no corpus/DEV/TEST.
